Cabinet Dispute Over Fossil Fuel Policy

Government insiders suggest that the Rosebank oilfield could be approved without violating UK climate targets, as emissions from exported oil do not count toward domestic carbon budgets. This technicality has sparked a divide within the Cabinet. While Energy Secretary Miatta Fahnbulleh has signaled reservations, Chancellor John Healey and other ministers advocate for approval, citing anticipated tax revenues and energy security.

Impact and Environmental Concerns

Climate campaigners and researchers note that while approval may not breach specific legal emission limits, it contradicts broader net-zero commitments. The decision follows a 2024 court ruling requiring ministers to consider emissions generated from burning extracted oil. Experts estimate the field could contribute significantly to emissions if fully developed. The government maintains that all decisions are subject to a rigorous, quasi-judicial process involving environmental assessments. Readers can review official policy updates at https://www.theguardian.com/environment/2026/oct/27/rosebank-oilfield-north-sea-uk-emissions-targets-insiders.
